root_cause.text: A race condition in the ublk driver where the async partition scan work can access ub->ub_disk after it has been freed during device teardown, because the work was not properly synchronized with the disk removal.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the race: ublk_ctrl_start_dev schedules partition_scan_work after add_disk; ublk_stop_dev calls del_gendisk, then ublk_detach_disk sets ub->ub_disk = NULL and put_disk may free the disk; the worker subsequently dereferences ub->ub_disk, leading to use-after-free. The patch fixes this by acquiring a disk reference via ublk_get_disk()/ublk_put_disk() in the worker and by replacing flush_work() with cancel_work_sync() to avoid running the work after the disk is detached.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the static function ublk_partition_scan_work as it is no longer used (dead code elimination).
intent_record.what: Removed the static function ublk_partition_scan_work, which was a work queue handler that used WARN_ON_ONCE, test_and_clear_bit, mutex_lock, bdev_disk_changed, and mutex_unlock.
intent_record.how: The function is deleted; any code that previously scheduled or invoked this work will no longer be able to do so, implying that partition scanning via this deferred work is removed or replaced.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a work function to scan partitions after clearing the suppress partition scan flag.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `ublk_partition_scan_work` that retrieves the gendisk, checks and clears `GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN`, locks the disk's open_mutex, calls `bdev_disk_changed(disk, false)` to rescan partitions, and releases the disk reference.
intent_record.how: Introduces a deferred workqueue handler for partition rescanning, ensuring proper synchronization and protection against use-after-free via `ublk_get_disk` and `ublk_put_disk`, and adds a debug warning if the suppression flag was not set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential unwanted partition scan execution on device stop by canceling rather than flushing the work.
intent_record.what: In function ublk_stop_dev, replaced flush_work(&ub->partition_scan_work) with cancel_work_sync(&ub->partition_scan_work).
intent_record.how: Instead of waiting for any pending partition scan work to complete, the new code cancels the work if it is still pending (i.e., not yet started) and waits for completion only if it is already executing. This prevents the partition scan from running when the device is being stopped.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the static function ublk_partition_scan_work as it is no longer used (dead code elimination).
Add a work function to scan partitions after clearing the suppress partition scan flag.
Fix potential unwanted partition scan execution on device stop by canceling rather than flushing the work.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the ublk_partition_scan_work function, which is the exact async partition scan work that caused the race condition by accessing freed ub_disk. Eliminating this dead code prevents the race condition from occurring.

The group adds a work function to scan partitions after clearing a suppress flag, but does not address the race condition where the partition scan work accesses freed ub->ub_disk during device teardown. The core intent does not involve synchronization with disk removal or preventing use-after-free.
The group's change directly addresses the race condition by canceling the partition scan work instead of flushing it, preventing the work from accessing the freed disk after device teardown.

candidates.rationale: This call only waits for currently running work but does not prevent the work from being re-queued later, allowing a partition scan work to run after ub->ub_disk has been freed during teardown.
Directly accesses ub->ub_disk->state in the work function, which can occur after ub->ub_disk has been freed if the work executes during device teardown, causing a use-after-free.
This call operates on ub->ub_disk inside the work function; if the work runs after the disk has been freed, it will access freed memory, leading to a use-after-free.
Acquires a lock on a mutex inside ub->ub_disk after the disk may have been freed, causing use-after-free when the work executes concurrently with disk removal.

vuln_statements.explanation: Direct access to ub->ub_disk->state inside the partition scan work function, which can occur after ub->ub_disk has been freed, leading to use-after-free.
Acquires a mutex lock on ub->ub_disk->open_mutex inside the work function, which may operate on freed memory if the work executes concurrently with disk removal.
Calls bdev_disk_changed with ub->ub_disk as argument inside the work function, which accesses the freed disk structure if the work runs after teardown.
Uses flush_work which only waits for currently running work but does not cancel pending re-queues, allowing the partition scan work to run after ub->ub_disk has been freed.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
ublk: scan partition in async way

Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
tables. Simila
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7fc4da6a304bdcd3de14fc946dc2c19437a9cc5a
Author: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Dec 23 11:27:40 2025 +0800

    ublk: scan partition in async way
    
    Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
    tables. Similar to nvme_partition_scan_work(), partition scanning is
    deferred to a work queue to prevent deadlocks.
    
    When partition scan happens synchronously during add_disk(), IO errors
    can cause the partition scan to wait while hold
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the async partition scan work and immediately adds proper synchronization via flush_work() in ublk_stop_dev() before disk cleanup. The work function accesses ub->ub_disk, but the flush ensures that any pending work completes before the disk is freed, preventing the race condition described in the root cause. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present but the fix is already in place.
